question: A kiln's measured gear backlash varies strongly at the same four marked shell positions across successive shutdowns. What should an agent test before suggesting a pinion move?
scenario: Girth gear clearance varies by kiln angle
evidence_required: backlash by marked circumferential station and measurement method
radial and axial runout at matching stations
tooth contact pattern and pinion bearing/base movement
kiln hot/cold state and historical alignment report
answer_and_decision_guide: Plot backlash and both runout components against identical kiln stations, then compare contact marks and support movement. If tight clearance follows gear eccentricity, moving the pinion to fix one position could worsen another; require gear/OEM alignment review and isolation before adjustments.

question: A contractor reports acceptable backlash at one position but edge-loaded tooth contact across the girth gear. What acceptance evidence should a buyer agent demand before approving the alignment invoice?

tooth contact pattern photographs under defined test condition
pinion angular alignment and bearing condition

answer_and_decision_guide: Do not accept one clearance reading as evidence of correct alignment. Require repeatable multi-station geometry, contact-pattern evidence, calibrated instruments and a documented comparison with the exact gear/OEM limits; escalate contradictory results before release or payment.

question: A kiln girth-gear spray system uses its usual lubricant quantity yet leaves a dry band at one tooth-flank edge. How should an agent separate nozzle distribution from mechanical contact problems?
scenario: Normal bulk consumption with local dry tooth band
evidence_required: per-nozzle cycle/pressure and delivery observations
safe photographic spray coverage across tooth width
tooth-flank temperature and contact pattern
lubricant condition, filter state and recent nozzle work
answer_and_decision_guide: Compare each nozzle's actual spray footprint rather than reservoir consumption alone. A missing or misdirected branch points toward delivery; even coverage with persistent hot edge contact points toward alignment or load distribution. Follow guarded/OEM inspection procedures; do not increase total dosage without isolating the cause.

question: A chain bucket elevator repeatedly reaches its take-up limit while measured chain pitch elongation remains low. What alternative faults should an agent investigate?
category: Bucket elevator take-up versus chain wear
scenario: Elevator take-up near end of travel despite low elongation
evidence_required: chain length over a fixed count of pitches at several locations
left/right take-up travel and symmetry
head and boot sprocket tooth/contact photographs
bucket attachments, casing rub and shaft alignment
answer_and_decision_guide: Verify pitch measurements against nominal chain geometry and OEM wear limits; compare both take-up sides and sprocket seating. Misalignment, sprocket wear, incorrect initial take-up or damaged attachments can mimic chain stretch. Isolate and secure the hanging assembly before physical inspection; do not prescribe chain replacement from take-up position alone.

question: A cement rotary airlock has a tight rotor-to-housing gap on one side and a wide gap opposite it. What should an agent test before ordering a new rotor?
scenario: Asymmetric tip clearance after a bearing service
evidence_required: feeler-gauge clearance map across blades and angular stations
shaft runout and bearing play
housing/endplate geometry and rub marks
operating temperature, material and differential-pressure history
answer_and_decision_guide: Map both tip and end clearances at isolated safe positions. Check bearing seating, shaft eccentricity, thermal distortion and housing damage before attributing the asymmetry to rotor wear. Compare to the specific OEM design and safety requirements; a new rotor may not cure a distorted housing.

question: A bag-filter hopper bridges mainly after long shutdowns, although its differential pressure during normal operation is stable. How should an agent test the discharge-sequence hypothesis?
scenario: Dust packs in hopper after shutdown/restart
evidence_required: fan, pulse and hopper-discharge PLC event timestamps
hopper level and residual dust after shutdown
rotary valve/screw operation and interlock logs
ambient/dew-point and dust moisture observations
answer_and_decision_guide: Reconstruct whether discharge equipment stops before residual dust can fall from bags and clear the hopper. Compare event sequence and material condition with a non-bridging shift, then inspect the discharge mechanism under isolation. A sequencing fault is a hypothesis; modify PLC logic only through the plant's approved controls and OEM process review.

question: A cement bag-filter hopper is bridged after humid nights and the maintenance team proposes a larger rotary valve. Which evidence should distinguish moisture caking from insufficient discharge capacity?
evidence_required: hopper dust moisture and temperature/dew-point trends
discharge rate versus peak dust load and pulse sequence
rotary valve clearances, leakage and motor load
hopper insulation, air ingress and wall deposit observations
answer_and_decision_guide: Check condensation, false-air paths and dust cohesiveness alongside the actual discharge duty. If caking is linked to dew point or stagnant deposits, greater nominal valve capacity may not help. Compare measured peak solids load with valve duty only after material and leakage causes are evaluated; do not install vibration or resize without structural/OEM review.

question: A vertical roller mill's grinding-pressure trace oscillates after a hydraulic service, and the nitrogen accumulator is blamed. What evidence should an agent require before authorizing gas charging?

accumulator OEM type, gas pre-charge history and service record
hydraulic valve/sensor calibration and oil temperature

answer_and_decision_guide: Correlate pressure fluctuations with feed changes, sensor drift and hydraulic-valve behavior before blaming the accumulator. question: A two-chamber cement mill loses throughput while its diaphragm differential pressure rises and coarse material accumulates in the first chamber. What evidence separates slot plugging from an upstream feed or ventilation change?
scenario: Rising interchamber restriction and low mill output
evidence_required: feed moisture and particle-size trends
chamber material sampling and grinding-media condition
mill ventilation flow/pressure and filter condition
isolated diaphragm slot photographs, open area and wear history
answer_and_decision_guide: Compare material transport and air-flow evidence before assuming the diaphragm needs larger slots. Wet fines, plugged grates, altered feed and ventilation loss can produce similar symptoms. Inspect internally only after full isolation; compare slot/open-area geometry with the original mill design, not generic internet dimensions.

question: A contractor proposes a different cement mill intermediate diaphragm because its quoted open area is larger. What should an AI buyer agent include in the technical acceptance criteria?
scenario: Higher-open-area diaphragm proposed for an existing tube mill
evidence_required: original chamber dimensions, mill design and material-flow duty
slot distribution, plate thickness, alloy and fixing drawings
media-retention and ventilation calculations
OEM-approved installation and post-restart performance test
answer_and_decision_guide: Assess media retention, material flow, ventilation, mechanical strength and wear life together. Larger open area alone does not prove better grinding performance and may change chamber hold-up or ball migration. Require dimensioned drawings, material certificates and OEM/engineering approval, then document safe trial acceptance before any order.
